text:
lara: noticed a spike of 500+ support tickets this morning — users reporting they can log in but their roles are missing or downgraded. started after yesterday's RBAC rename deploy. :grimacing:

sam: ouch. which attribute are we mapping for roles now?

lara: we changed Okta SAML mapping from `roles` -> `entitlements_v2` to support scoping. rollout was staged but config landed in prod for a subset of apps.

jules: hmm we also rotated the KMS key used for decrypting encrypted SAML assertions at 03:10 UTC. Could that line up? :thinking_face:

lara: timeline: deploy 02:45 UTC (rbac rename + console mapping), KMS rotate 03:10, first tickets 03:18. seems suspicious.

okta-bot: SCIM provisioning events: 03:12 user:j.doe failed attribute parsing (missing `eduPersonPrincipalName`) - error code 422.

sam: so two parallel failures: attribute rename -> mapping mismatch, and decryption/key rotate causing assertions to be unreadable -> fallback to creating accounts without entitlements.

alex: quick check — can we paste the current mapping snippet?

jules: sure, from IdP app settings:

```
Attribute statements (SAML):
- Name: entitlement
  NameFormat: urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:attrname-format:unspecified
  Value: user.entitlements_v2
- Name: eduPersonPrincipalName
  Value: user.eppn
```

lara: and the platform RBAC now expects `entitlements_v2` in the decoded assertion. If assertion can't be decrypted we get an empty map and fallback role applied (read-only).

marta: users getting admin removed — that's good (least privilege) — but some internal service accounts ended up downgraded and triggered failures. we need a fast mitigation.

sam: mitigation options: rollback mapping rename, rollback KMS rotation (not ideal), or add a temporary fallback that maps `roles` -> `entitlements_v2` if missing.

alex: can we enable a one-off canary that accepts both `roles` and `entitlements_v2` in the mapping? low-risk and fast.

jules: yes I can update the app mapping in Okta to include both names; takes ~5m to push. but need to confirm KMS decryption is stable — otherwise some assertions still empty.

lara: please also add expanded audit logging for any auth path that produced a fallback role so we can enumerate affected users. add fields: saml_present, decrypted:boolean, mapped_attr_names.

marta: also add an alert: if >50 fallback_role grants in 15m, page EngSec and Oncall.

okta-bot: audit link: <https://okta.company.com/admin/audit|Okta org audit> (filtered for app: redwood-console)

sam: jules — before you change mappings, can you confirm whether rotated KMS key is in keyring and accessible by the decryptor? last rotation job showed one host failed to update key ARN.

jules: checking hosts... looks like the decryption microservice on host infra-gpu-03 didn't pick up the new key ARN due to stale env reload. patching now.

lara: timeline for fixes: jules patch + okta mapping update immediately, sam adds audit log, alex adds alert. after that we can evaluate if a rollback is needed.

marta: nice, also open a short postmortem ticket and tag Customer Success to proactively reach out to impacted customers.

sam: adding a temporary migration in the auth layer to check for old claim name `roles` and choose highest privilege between claims. will log all decisions.

jules: mapping updated and infra-gpu-03 env reloaded — I see decryption success rate jump in logs: 98% -> 99.7%.

okta-bot: SCIM provisioning events: 03:46 reconciled 212 users (attribute parse fixed).

lara: great. leave the temporary multiple-claim mapping in place for 48h and monitor audit. I'll open the PM/incident doc. :memo:

marta: noted. I'll draft customer comms with CS. :email:

sam: follow-ups: add unit tests around missing-claim behavior, and include KMS rotation verification in deploy checklist.

lara: agreed. thanks everyone — closing loop once postmortem is up. :thumbsup:
